READABILITY.evidence: Names reveal intent (unionConsistentHash, suppressed, clone). Comments explain merge priority, e.g. "p2 is higher priority than p1, except disable on narrower-scoped p1 suppresses inherited p2". API types are documented and formatting matches the repo.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: Fits the plugin pattern: a new consistent_hash.go, wired into constructor.go and traffic_policy_plugin.go, with mergeConsistentHash registered. But mergeConsistentHash is ~55 lines, and its disable/suppressed checks are repeated in both strategy branches of the switch.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: constructConsistentHash returns errors that are collected in ConstructIR. A Validate() step is registered. MinLength=1 markers sit on key fields. Unsupported merge strategies log a warning. Clone avoids sharing IR state across routes.

C7-11-CASE1.evidence: mergeConsistentHash is registered in MergeTrafficPolicies. It unions entries with the higher-priority policy first via unionConsistentHash and handles disable/suppressed. It records origins with mergeOrigins.SetOne/Append("consistentHash"), and TrafficPolicyMergeOpts gains a ConsistentHash field. Hidden tests pass.

C7-11-CASE2.evidence: A CEL rule on the ConsistentHash type ("when disable is true, no other fields may be set") appears in the generated CRD YAML and is covered by TestConsistentHashCRDValidation. Disable suppresses inherited policies through the suppressed flag, including the three-level test case. The empty {} spec is handled, and hidden tests pass.
